qbi_deduction.citation: IRS Qualified Business Income Deduction page describes Section 199A. Rev. Proc. 2025-32 sets 2026 taxable-income thresholds and upper phase-in range amounts for Section 199A.

wage_ubia_limit.citation: IRS Qualified Business Income Deduction guidance describes the W-2 wage and unadjusted basis immediately after acquisition (UBIA) limitations that can apply to Section 199A deductions above the taxable-income threshold.

qbi_deduction.notes: Below the taxable-income threshold, the core QBI deduction can be modeled as the lesser of 20% of qualified business income or 20% of taxable income minus net capital gain. For 2026, Rev. Proc. 2025-32 and OBBBA-era inflation guidance place single/head_of_household/qualifying_surviving_spouse in the All Other Returns row ($201,750 to $276,750), married_filing_separately at $201,775 to $276,775, and married_filing_jointly at $403,500 to $553,500. Above the threshold and through the upper limit, W-2 wage, UBIA, and SSTB phase-in rules require business-specific inputs. Above the upper limit, those limitations fully apply.
qbi_deduction.rev_proc_2024_40_filing_status_mapping_n: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 lists Section 199A rows for Married Filing Jointly, Married Filing Separately, and All Other Returns. single, head_of_household, and qualifying_surviving_spouse are mapped to All Other Returns.
